statement: Every selected union of original open plane loop-group orbits has one compact path-connected labelled family K of actual global operator-centralizing maps whose two-letter evaluation contains a neighborhood of every point. For a fixed-frontier union with zero-dimensional full local centralizers, arbitrary locally finite disjoint operator orbits of sufficiently small disks support an actual topological embedding of the product of their boundary-fixed homeomorphism groups into the global operator centralizer. Its maps and inverses extend continuously across every frontier accumulation with the uniform bound (K K^-1)^2, and its image has the explicit product Alexander contraction.
depends_on: C30 precise Polish orbit-open-map theorem and exact stabilizer restriction kernel; C32 closed original source lifts; C33 free proper Lie local centralizers; C63 closed compatible tuple topology; proved complete-source compact-lifting construction; exact Alexander formula
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and controlled localization at fixed frontiers
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Every original source-cover label is retained in the compact controlling family, and every actual operator restriction kernel is retained in the localization map.
notes: The based path group in the exact closed compatible group is Polish and acts transitively by endpoints. Open evaluation gives compact lifts of small closed disks through a fully proved nested source-ball and compact target-shrinking construction, with no continuous endpoint section assumed. A countable exhaustion and families tending uniformly to identity produce one compact labelled family K. Small disk translates are disjoint by freeness and properness of the effective discrete stabilizer. The disks are representatives of distinct operator orbits. For any two points in a disk, the four-letter family (K K^-1)^2 relates them, and this estimate survives every operator translate. Since this family fixes the frontier, all pasted maps and inverses are jointly continuous uniformly over the entire product of disk homeomorphisms. Restriction gives the continuous inverse to the group embedding. The displayed Alexander map contracts each factor, fixes the identity and has its stated inverse. No factorization of an arbitrary original loop into this contractible subgroup, no simultaneous graph deformation, and no extension over nonfixed frontiers is asserted; these remain C12 obligations.
